notes: Numbers are published research / MSU Extension reference values. Field scouting always overrides the model.

simple.name: Simple chill hours
simple.source: Common 32–45°F band used for tart cherry; README cites 1200+ hours for many MI tart blocks

utah.name: Utah model (Richardson 1974)
utah.source: Anderson et al. 1986 / Zavalloni phenology work: 954 chill units for Montmorency

zavalloni.name: Zavalloni (base 4°C from 1 Mar)
zavalloni.source: Zavalloni et al. 2006, J. Amer. Soc. Hort. Sci. 131:601–607

msu_base42.name: MSU Enviroweather-style (base 42°F from 1 Jan)
msu_base42.source: MSU Extension NW Michigan fruit reports: tart cherry full bloom ~360 GDD base 42

post_chill.name: Post-chill GDD (base 41°F after chill met)
post_chill.source: README / typical 230–250 GDD after chill for Montmorency bloom

frost.note: Critical temperatures are approximate killing temps at 10% injury for the current stage. Use MSU critical-temperature sheets for spray/wind-machine decisions.

pest_watch_windows.name: Plum curculio
pest_watch_windows.timing: Petal fall through shuck split; activity increases as temps warm after bloom
pest_watch_windows.note: Use the Enviroweather model. This dashboard does not recommend sprays.

pest_watch_windows.name: Cherry leaf spot
pest_watch_windows.timing: From petal fall through harvest whenever leaf-wetness + temperature thresholds are met
pest_watch_windows.note: Infection periods are wetness-driven. Link is pre-filtered to Williamsburg.

pest_watch_windows.name: Spotted wing drosophila
pest_watch_windows.timing: Fruit coloring / ~530 GDD base 4°C onward for tart cherry susceptibility (MSU prototype risk model)
pest_watch_windows.note: Color change is the field trigger. GDD is a planning aid only.
